# Loading R package

Installing catchment R package from github

Use the code chunk below to install catchment R package from github.

```{r}
install.packages("remotes")
```

```{r}
remotes::install_github('uva-bi-sdad/catchment')
```

Next, load sf, tidyverse, tmap, accessibility and catchment R packages into RStudio environment using the code chunk below

```{r}
pacman::p_load(sf, tidyverse, tmap, accessibility, catchment)
```

# Importing geospatial data: mpsz, hexagons and ELDERCARE

```{r}
mpsz <- st_read(dsn = "data/geospatial",
                layer = "MP14_SUBZONE_NO_SEA_PL") %>%
  st_transform(crs = 3414)
```

```{r}
hexagons <- st_read(dsn = "data/geospatial",
                    layer = "hexagons") %>%
  st_transform(crs = 3414)
```

```{r}
eldercare <- st_read(dsn = "data/geospatial",
                     layer = "ELDERCARE") %>%
  st_transform(crs = 3414)
```

Next, use the code chunk below to import OD_Matrix.

```{r}
ODMatrix <- read_csv("data/aspatial/OD_Matrix.csv", skip = 0)
```

**Observation.** The spatial layers and OD table describe the same accessibility system. EPSG:3414 puts the data in metres, which makes the distance threshold meaningful.

Use the code chunk below to create a new field called demand and populate value 100 in it.

```{r}
hexagons <- hexagons %>%
  select(fid) %>%
  mutate(demand = 100) %>%
  rename(id = fid)
```

Use the code chunk the select origin_id, destination_id and total_cost of ODMatrix data frame. Then, rename them to from_id, to_id and dist respectively.

```{r}
ODMatrix_tidied <- ODMatrix %>%
  select(origin_id, destination_id, total_cost) %>%
  rename(from_id = origin_id,
         to_id = destination_id,
         dist = total_cost)
```

In the code chunk below as.matrix() is used to convert the data frame into matrix object.

```{r}
distmat <- ODMatrix %>%
  select(origin_id, destination_id, total_cost) %>%
  spread(destination_id, total_cost) %>%
  select(c(-c('origin_id')))

distmat_km <- as.matrix(distmat/1000)
```

In this code chunk below, catchment_ratio() of catchment package is used to compute 2SFCA.

```{r}
eldercare <- eldercare %>%
  mutate(capacity = 100)
```

```{r}
df_2sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand,
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  max_cost = 5) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("2SFCA" = ".")
```

# Mapping 2SFCA

```{r}
mapex <- st_bbox(hexagons)
```

```{r}
hex_2SFCA <- bind_cols(hexagons, df_2sfca)
tm_shape(hex_2SFCA,
         bbox = mapex) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "2SFCA",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
                style = "quantile",
                n = 10,
                values = "-brewer.blues")) +
tm_shape(eldercare) +
  tm_dots(size = 0.3,
          fill = "red",
          col = "black") +
  tm_title("2SFCA Accessibility measures") +
  tm_layout(frame = TRUE) +
  tm_compass(type="8star", size = 2) +
  tm_scalebar() +
tm_grid(alpha = 0.2)
```

**Observation.** The 2SFCA map shows relative access within five kilometres. Darker areas have more nearby supply compared with demand, while the red points show provider locations.

# Enhanced 2-Step Floating Catchment Area (E2SFCA)

```{r}
step_weights <- list(c(5, .01), c(4, .05), c(3, .1), c(2, .4), c(1, 1))
df_e2sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand,
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  weight = step_weights) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("E2SFCA" = ".")
```

```{r}
hex_E2SFCA <- bind_cols(hexagons, df_e2sfca)
tm_shape(hex_E2SFCA,
         bbox = mapex) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "E2SFCA",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
                style = "quantile",
                n = 10,
                values = "-brewer.blues")) +
tm_shape(eldercare) +
  tm_dots(size = 0.3,
          fill = "red",
          col = "black") +
  tm_title("E2SFCA Accessibility measures") +
  tm_layout(frame = TRUE) +
  tm_compass(type="8star", size = 2) +
  tm_scalebar() +
tm_grid(alpha = 0.2)
```

**Observation.** E2SFCA gives more weight to closer providers. It therefore shows local differences more clearly than the simple five-kilometre cut-off.

# Kernel Density (Gaussian) 2-Step Floating Catchment Area

```{r}
df_kd2sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand,
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  weight = "gaussian") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("KD2SFCA" = ".")
```

```{r}
hex_KD2SFCA <- bind_cols(hexagons, df_kd2sfca)
tm_shape(hex_KD2SFCA,
         bbox = mapex) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "KD2SFCA",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
                style = "quantile",
                n = 10,
                values = "-brewer.blues")) +
tm_shape(eldercare) +
  tm_dots(size = 0.3,
          fill = "red",
          col = "black") +
  tm_title("KD2SFCA Accessibility measures") +
  tm_layout(frame = TRUE) +
  tm_compass(type="8star", size = 2) +
  tm_scalebar() +
  tm_grid(alpha = 0.2)
```

**Observation.** KD2SFCA uses a smooth Gaussian distance decay. The accessibility pattern changes more gradually instead of stopping sharply at the catchment boundary.

# 3-Step Floating Catchment Area

```{r}
df_3sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand,
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  step_weights,
  normalize_weight = TRUE) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("3SFCA" = ".")
```

```{r}
hex_3SFCA <- bind_cols(hexagons, df_3sfca)
tm_shape(hex_3SFCA,
         bbox = mapex) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "3SFCA",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
                style = "quantile",
                n = 10,
                values = "-brewer.blues")) +
tm_shape(eldercare) +
  tm_dots(size = 0.3,
          fill = "red",
          col = "black") +
  tm_title("3SFCA Accessibility measures") +
  tm_layout(frame = TRUE) +
  tm_compass(type="8star", size = 2) +
  tm_scalebar() +
  tm_grid(alpha = 0.2)
```

**Observation.** The 3SFCA map uses normalized distance weights. Areas that remain high across the four maps are more stable areas of good accessibility.

## Overall observation

These methods use different distance assumptions, so their values should be compared as relative accessibility patterns. The results also depend on the five-kilometre limit and the assumed demand and capacity values.
